segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: Hi guys.
segments.zh: 大家好。

segments.en: My name is Katherine and today we have an upper intermediate level lesson for you about some very interesting things.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们为您准备了一节中高级课程，聊一些非常有趣的东西。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today we're going to talk about fortune tellers or people that read your future.
segments.zh: 今天我们要聊的是算命先生，也就是帮你预测未来的人。

segments.en: Alright so if I want to know who I will marry, if I will be rich, I will go to this fortune teller and she or he will tell me what's in my future.
segments.zh: 好吧，比如我想知道我会和谁结婚、会不会发财，我就会去找算命先生，他或她就会告诉我未来会怎样。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: It's very popular in many cultures around the world, many different ways of reading your future or telling you your future.
segments.zh: 它在世界各地许多文化中都很流行，预知未来、预言未来的方式五花八门。

segments.en: So let's jump into this dialogue and see what's going on today.
segments.zh: 所以让我们跳进这个对话，看看今天发生了什么。

segments.en: Look at this newspaper article about this famous local medium.
segments.zh: 看这篇报纸文章，写的是本地一位有名的通灵师。

segments.en: It says that she is really gifted and so popular now that she's booked solid with appointments for the next 12 months.
segments.zh: 文章说她很有本事，如今人气高得不得了，接下来十二个月的预约都排满了。

segments.en: You don't really believe in all that hocus pocus mumbo jumbo do you?
segments.zh: 你不会真相信这些装神弄鬼、胡说八道的东西吧？

segments.en: Well I have had many friends that went to a psychic and got their palms read and most of the things the psychic told them came true.
segments.zh: 我有不少朋友找灵媒看过手相，对方说的大多数事情后来都应验了。

segments.en: Of course it does.
segments.zh: 当然会应验啦。

segments.en: They tell you general and obvious things like that you'll be successful or have a big house.
segments.zh: 他们只会说些笼统又显而易见的话，比如你会成功、会住上大房子。

segments.en: I think most of the times they're just scam artists.
segments.zh: 我觉得他们多半是骗子。

segments.en: Well historically it's a practice that many cultures share.
segments.zh: 不过从历史上看，许多文化都有占卜的传统。

segments.en: Reading the tarot cards.
segments.zh: 比如用塔罗牌占卜。

segments.en: In the east they would even read tea leaves.
segments.zh: 在东方，人们甚至会用茶叶渣占卜。

segments.en: I even heard that there are people that make you smoke a cigar and then read your ashes.
segments.zh: 我还听说，有人会让你抽一支雪茄，再根据烟灰占卜。

segments.en: All superstitious nonsense.
segments.zh: 全是迷信的胡说八道。

segments.en: I would still like to go to one and see what he or she has to say just for kicks.
segments.zh: 我还是想找一个试试，看对方会说些什么，就当图个乐子。

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: I'll make an appointment.
segments.zh: 我会预约的。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We're back.
segments.zh: 我们回来了。

segments.en: So a lot of interesting things here.
segments.zh: 这里有很多有趣的事情。

segments.en: Let's take a look at some of those words on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 让我们来看看语言要点中的一些词。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: So in Language Takeaway today we are focusing on some words that describe fortune telling but also the different ways of doing so.
segments.zh: 因此，在今天的语言要点中，我们专注于一些描述算命的词，以及这样做的不同方式。

segments.en: The first word we have is actually a name for a person who can read the future.
segments.zh: 我们的第一个词其实是指能预知未来的人的一个称呼。

segments.en: Right Marco?
segments.zh: 正确的马可？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: A medium.
segments.zh: 灵媒。

segments.en: In the dialogue we hear about a woman who is a medium and is very talented.
segments.zh: 在对话中，我们听到一个女人是灵媒，而且很有天赋。

segments.en: Actually a medium is interesting because a medium is a person who can communicate with the dead.
segments.zh: 其实灵媒很有意思，因为灵媒就是能与死者交流的人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Or who can communicate with the other side.
segments.zh: 或者谁可以与对方交流。

segments.en: But if you think about middle, medium, I mean they mean the same thing.
segments.zh: 但如果你想想 middle、medium，它们的意思其实一样。

segments.en: It's someone who is in the middle of two things.
segments.zh: 这是一个处于两件事中间的人。

segments.en: And so a medium can maybe transmit these different ideas or signals.
segments.zh: 因此，媒介可能可以传递这些不同的想法或信号。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So it's a person that basically communicates as you say with the dead or someone that can listen to people who are not here anymore.
segments.zh: 所以，正如你所说，这种人基本上就是与死者交流的人，或者能听到已经不在人世的人说话的人。

segments.en: But obviously they are a type of person that could also use this gift to tell your future or to have the people who are dead tell you what's going to happen in the future.
segments.zh: 但显然他们这种人也能用这份天赋来告诉你未来，或者让死去的人告诉你将来会发生什么。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And so another kind of person who would do something similar is a psychic.
segments.zh: 所以另一种会做类似事情的人是通灵者。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Alright now a psychic is a person who generally will read your future for you, will tell you the future.
segments.zh: 好，通灵者通常是会为你预知未来、告诉你将来会发生什么的人。

segments.en: Maybe the psychic will have a special tool like a crystal ball.
segments.zh: 也许通灵者会有一个特殊的工具，比如水晶球。

segments.en: Just remember that in English, psych, like psychology, psychosis has to do with your mind.
segments.zh: 请记住，在英语中，psych 这个词根，像 psychology（心理学）、psychosis（精神病）一样，都和心智有关。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a psychic uses their mind to find out things about you or your future.
segments.zh: 所以通灵者用他们的心智来了解你或你的未来。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So sometimes psychics will claim that they can read your mind as well.
segments.zh: 所以有时通灵者会声称他们也可以读懂你的想法。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: It's a little scary.
segments.zh: 这有点吓人。

segments.en: So as you say, these are different, these are people who supposedly can tell you your future.
segments.zh: 所以正如你所说，这些是不同的，这些人应该可以告诉你你的未来。

segments.en: And as you said, they use different methods or different tools.
segments.zh: 正如你所说，他们使用不同的方法或不同的工具。

segments.en: One of them is for example having your palms read.
segments.zh: 其中之一就是看手相。

segments.en: Alright, so the psychic will go to you Marco and will look at your hand and will read your palm.
segments.zh: 好，所以通灵师会走到你面前，马可，看着你的手，为你看手相。

segments.en: Now where on your hand is your palm?
segments.zh: 现在你手上的手掌在哪里？

segments.en: It's on the other side, the side where you grab things with.
segments.zh: 它在另一边，你拿东西的那一边。

segments.en: The inside, so the soft part.
segments.zh: 里面，所以柔软的部分。

segments.en: And maybe on your palm you have many different lines.
segments.zh: 也许在你的手掌上你有许多不同的线条。

segments.en: So the psychic will look at the lines and will say, oh well this line is very long, so you will have a long, long life.
segments.zh: 所以通灵者会看线条，会说，哦，这条线很长，所以你的寿命很长。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So maybe in your hands you have lines that determine how much money you will have or how many kids you will have or how long you will live.
segments.zh: 所以也许你手上的掌纹决定了你会有多少钱、有几个孩子，或者能活多久。

segments.en: So that's called a palm reading.
segments.zh: 所以这就叫看手相。

segments.en: Or I am going to have my palm read.
segments.zh: 或者说我要让人给我看手相。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Now the other person doesn't really believe in all that stuff and says that they are just scam artists.
segments.zh: 现在另一个人并不真正相信所有这些东西，并说他们只是骗子。

segments.en: So he's saying that the psychics or the mediums are just scam artists.
segments.zh: 所以他说通灵者或媒介只是骗子。

segments.en: Alright, so what is a scam artist?
segments.zh: 好，那什么是 scam artist（骗子）？

segments.en: Well a scam artist is not a real artist.
segments.zh: 好吧，骗子不是真正的艺术家。

segments.en: A scam artist is a thief, someone who will maybe tell you a story or who will lie to you to try and take your money.
segments.zh: 骗子是小偷，他可能会告诉你一个故事，或者会骗你试图拿走你的钱。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So he's not really like a robber, like somebody that will break into your house and take your things.
segments.zh: 所以他不像一个强盗，就像一个会闯入你家并拿走你的东西的人。

segments.en: No, he won't use a gun, maybe, hopefully not, but he will tell you a story or will lie to you in a way that makes you want to give him money.
segments.zh: 不，他不会使用枪，也许，希望不会，但他会告诉你一个故事，或者会以一种让你想给他钱的方式对你撒谎。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So I don't know if any of you have ever received an email from someone who said, I am a wealthy person from a different part of the world and I want you to give me money to help me so I can come to America and these kinds of things where you don't know the person, he's probably lying to you, it's a very sad story.
segments.zh: 所以我不知道你们有没有人收到过这样的邮件，对方说：我是来自世界某个地方的富人，希望你们给我钱帮我，好让我能去美国，诸如此类；你根本不认识这个人，他很可能在骗你，这是个很可悲的故事。

segments.en: I say please give me money so I can come to visit you or so I can come and have a good life.
segments.zh: 我说请给我钱，这样我就可以来拜访你，这样我就可以来过上美好的生活。

segments.en: That's a scam artist.
segments.zh: 那是骗子。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: People probably don't have a bad life, they just want you to give them money.
segments.zh: 人们可能没有糟糕的生活，他们只是想让你给他们钱。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So that is a scam artist.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个骗子。

segments.en: And well he went on to say about how all of these things, about fortune telling, about psychics and everything is just superstitious nonsense.
segments.zh: 他接着说，所有这些东西——算命、通灵之类的——都只是迷信的胡说八道。

segments.en: So then the girl went on to explain and saying that it's not really true that many cultures do things like, for example, read the tarot cards.
segments.zh: 于是女孩接着解释，说其实并非如此，许多文化都会做类似的事，比如用塔罗牌占卜。

segments.en: Alright so we had palm reading first, maybe talking to dead people with a medium.
segments.zh: 好，我们刚才先说了看手相，也许还提到通过灵媒与死人交谈。

segments.en: But this is another tool that psychics use to communicate with maybe the dead or to understand the future.
segments.zh: 但这是通灵者用来与死者交流或了解未来的另一个工具。

segments.en: So we have tarot cards and they're actually cards, like playing cards, but they're a little bit different, right?
segments.zh: 所以我们有塔罗牌，它们实际上是牌，就像扑克牌，但它们有点不同，对吧？

segments.en: They don't have diamonds and hearts, they have different pictures.
segments.zh: 它们没有方块和红桃，而是有不同的图案。

segments.en: Right, they have pictures of, for example, a king or a queen or a picture of a river or different symbols that basically the person who is getting their fortune read will take it and move them and shuffle them and then will start flipping the cards over and then you will see supposedly what your future will be like.
segments.zh: 对，上面有图案，比如国王、王后，或者一条河，或者各种符号；基本上，来算命的人会拿起牌、洗牌，然后开始翻牌，接着你就会看到据说你未来的样子。

segments.en: Alright so those are tarot cards.
segments.zh: 好吧，那些是塔罗牌。

segments.en: But we have one more word here and it actually comes from the friend who doesn't believe in these scam artists.
segments.zh: 但我们这里还有一个词，它其实出自那个不相信这些骗子的朋友。

segments.en: It calls it all superstitious nonsense.
segments.zh: 他说这些全是迷信的胡说八道。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So a person that is superstitious believes in superstitions and those are beliefs of good or bad luck.
segments.zh: 所以一个迷信的人相信迷信，这些信念是好运或厄运的信念。

segments.en: Yeah that's right.
segments.zh: 是的，没错。

segments.en: So if I believe that the number 13 is very very bad, I will avoid the number 13.
segments.zh: 所以如果我相信13号是非常非常糟糕的，我会避开13号。

segments.en: I won't sit down in chair number 13, I won't buy a house on floor number 13 because I'm superstitious.
segments.zh: 我不会坐在 13 号椅子上，我不会在 13 楼买房子，因为我很迷信。

segments.en: I believe that that number is bad luck.
segments.zh: 我相信这个数字是厄运。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So many believe that it's bad luck to break a mirror or to walk under a ladder.
segments.zh: 很多人认为打破镜子或在梯子下行走是不幸的。

segments.en: Yes, also many Americans believe it's bad luck to open an umbrella inside.
segments.zh: 是的，许多美国人也认为在里面打开雨伞是不好的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it's interesting because many cultures around the world have different types of superstitions but we'll talk about that in a little bit.
segments.zh: 所以这很有趣，因为世界各地的许多文化都有不同类型的迷信，但我们稍后会谈到这一点。

segments.en: Why don't we move on now to some fluency builder and take a look at some phrases.
segments.zh: 现在我们来看流利表达，看几个短语吧。

segments.en: Look at this newspaper article about this famous local medium.
segments.zh: 看这篇报纸文章，写的是本地一位有名的通灵师。

segments.en: It says that she is really gifted and so popular now that she's booked solid with appointments for the next 12 months.
segments.zh: 文章说她很有本事，如今人气高得不得了，接下来十二个月的预约都排满了。

segments.en: You don't really believe in all that hocus pocus mumbo jumbo do you?
segments.zh: 你不会真相信这些装神弄鬼、胡说八道的东西吧？

segments.en: Well I have had many friends that went to a psychic and got their palms read and most of the things the psychic told them came true.
segments.zh: 我有不少朋友找灵媒看过手相，对方说的大多数事情后来都应验了。

segments.en: Of course it does.
segments.zh: 当然会应验啦。

segments.en: They tell you general and obvious things like that you'll be successful or have a big house.
segments.zh: 他们只会说些笼统又显而易见的话，比如你会成功、会住上大房子。

segments.en: I think most of the times they're just scam artists.
segments.zh: 我觉得他们多半是骗子。

segments.en: Well historically it's a practice that many cultures share.
segments.zh: 不过从历史上看，许多文化都有占卜的传统。

segments.en: Reading the tarot cards.
segments.zh: 比如用塔罗牌占卜。

segments.en: In the east they would even read tea leaves.
segments.zh: 在东方，人们甚至会用茶叶渣占卜。

segments.en: I even heard that there are people that make you smoke a cigar and then read your ashes.
segments.zh: 我还听说，有人会让你抽一支雪茄，再根据烟灰占卜。

segments.en: All superstitious nonsense.
segments.zh: 全是迷信的胡说八道。

segments.en: I would still like to go to one and see what he or she has to say just for kicks.
segments.zh: 我还是想找一个试试，看对方会说些什么，就当图个乐子。

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: I'll book an appointment.
segments.zh: 我会预约。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: An important phrase that you don't have to be a psychic to use is booked solid.
segments.zh: 有一个重要短语，你不必是通灵者也能用，那就是 booked solid。

segments.en: Now we heard this in the beginning of the dialogue.
segments.zh: 现在我们在对话开始时听到了这一点。

segments.en: Right because this person is so famous that so many people want to go there and get their fortunes read that this person is already booked solid for the next 12 months.
segments.zh: 对，因为这个人太出名了，很多人想去找他算命，所以他接下来 12 个月的预约都排满了。

segments.en: Okay now booked solid is a very nice colloquial way to describe having no time for anything in English.
segments.zh: 好，booked solid 是一种很地道的口语说法，用来形容在英语里完全没时间做任何事。

segments.en: So basically if a restaurant for example is booked solid it means there are no tables available.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，比如一家餐厅 booked solid，意思就是没有空桌了。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Nothing is available.
segments.zh: 没有任何可用的。

segments.en: Everything is already reserved.
segments.zh: 一切都已经保留。

segments.en: Yeah it happens also with hotels.
segments.zh: 是的，它也发生在酒店。

segments.en: Some hotels during let's say the Olympics many of them are booked solid for the entire month.
segments.zh: 比如说奥运会期间，有些酒店整个月都订满了。

segments.en: Or you could even say this with your friends.
segments.zh: 或者你甚至可以和你的朋友说这句话。

segments.en: You say hey Marco do you want to hang out Thursday say 7 o'clock.
segments.zh: 你说嘿，马可，你想星期四出去玩，说 7 点钟。

segments.en: Sorry I'm booked solid the entire day.
segments.zh: 抱歉，我一整天都订满了。

segments.en: Popular guy.
segments.zh: 真是个红人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you can say that a person is booked solid or that a business is booked solid.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说某个人 booked solid，也可以说某家店 booked solid。

segments.en: Now this next phrase is kind of more it's not really real words but we say they are hocus pocus mumbo jumbo.
segments.zh: 下一个短语其实不太算真正的词，但我们说它们是 hocus pocus mumbo jumbo。

segments.en: Alright hocus pocus is a way to describe superstitious things.
segments.zh: 好吧，hocus pocus 是一种描述迷信事物的方式。

segments.en: Like magic right because I think it comes from supposedly it's a spell that witches or wizards will say like hocus pocus and things will appear.
segments.zh: 就像魔法一样，因为我认为它来自据说是女巫或巫师会说的咒语，就像 Hocus Pocus 一样，事情就会出现。

segments.en: Abracadabra.
segments.zh: 阿布拉卡达布拉。

segments.en: Hocus yeah.
segments.zh: Hocus，对。

segments.en: But basically this is something that we say when we're joking now in English.
segments.zh: 但基本上这是我们现在用英语开玩笑时所说的话。

segments.en: So I'll say oh gosh Marco I just broke this mirror.
segments.zh: 所以我会说哦，天哪，我刚刚打破了这面镜子。

segments.en: Seven years bad luck.
segments.zh: 七年运气不好。

segments.en: Do you really believe in all that hocus pocus?
segments.zh: 你真的相信那些装神弄鬼的东西吗？

segments.en: Yes I'm very superstitious.
segments.zh: 是的，我很迷信。

segments.en: So hocus pocus here means superstitious.
segments.zh: 所以这里的hocus pocus意味着迷信。

segments.en: Like magic superstitious stuff.
segments.zh: 就是魔法、迷信之类的东西。

segments.en: It's all hocus pocus.
segments.zh: 这都是 Hocus Pocus。

segments.en: What about mumbo jumbo?
segments.zh: 那 mumbo jumbo 呢？

segments.en: Mumbo jumbo is also something we say when we're talking about magic or things that are superstitious.
segments.zh: mumbo jumbo 也是我们谈论魔法或迷信事物时会说的词。

segments.en: So I can say I don't believe in any of that superstitious mumbo jumbo.

segments.en: I don't think it's true.

segments.en: I think it's silly.

segments.en: Right so mumbo jumbo you refer to that nonsense that irrational or unbelievable stuff.
segments.zh: 是的，胡说八道，你指的是那些不合理或令人难以置信的废话。

segments.en: So hocus referring to magic mumbo jumbo referring to superstition or things that are not really believable let's say.

segments.en: And to end the dialogue the guy says well you know what okay let's go to this psychic and see what she has to say just for kicks.

segments.zh: 现在我喜欢这句话。

segments.en: I use it a lot.
segments.zh: 我经常使用它。

segments.en: It's very very colloquial very spoken English so you guys should try to use it.
segments.zh: 这是非常非常口语化的英语，所以你们应该尝试使用它。

segments.en: It means just for fun.
segments.zh: 这意味着只是为了好玩。

segments.en: Just for fun.

segments.zh: 但我确实认为这会很有趣。

segments.en: So let's go just for kicks.

segments.en: Just for kicks.

segments.en: That's right.

segments.en: Maybe like if you just sit down and start doing some math problems just for kicks.
segments.zh: 比如你就是坐下来做几道数学题，图个乐。

segments.zh: 是的，你会那样做，不是吗？

segments.en: Just for kicks.

segments.en: Yeah.

segments.en: Or I'm going to take a singing class just for kicks even though I don't take singing very seriously.
segments.zh: 或者我去报个唱歌班，就图个乐，虽然我并不把唱歌当回事。

segments.en: Right.

segments.zh: 文章说她很有本事，如今人气高得不得了，接下来十二个月的预约都排满了。

segments.zh: 你不会真相信这些装神弄鬼、胡说八道的东西吧？

segments.en: Well I have had many friends that went to a psychic and got their palms read and most of the things the psychic told them came true.
segments.zh: 我有不少朋友找灵媒看过手相，对方说的大多数事情后来都应验了。

segments.en: Of course it does.
segments.zh: 当然会应验啦。

segments.en: They tell you general and obvious things like that you'll be successful or have a big house.
segments.zh: 他们只会说些笼统又显而易见的话，比如你会成功、会住上大房子。

segments.en: I think most of the times they're just scam artists.
segments.zh: 我觉得他们多半是骗子。

segments.zh: 不过从历史上看，许多文化都有占卜的传统。

segments.zh: 我还听说，有人会让你抽一支雪茄，再根据烟灰占卜。

segments.zh: 我还是想找一个试试，看对方会说些什么，就当图个乐子。

segments.zh: 所以说到迷信，正如你所说的，有些迷信更本地化。

segments.zh: 例如，我认为是美国人认为在房子里打开雨伞是厄运。

segments.en: I know that for example in China it's the number four is considered bad luck.
segments.zh: 我知道，比如在中国，数字四被认为不吉利。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you'll see that many buildings don't have a floor number four or 14.

segments.en: That's right.

segments.zh: 你的钱会飞走。

segments.zh: 你的钱会流失，或者你的钱会消失。

segments.zh: 所以女人不会把包或钱包放在地板上。

segments.zh: 这就是为什么你总是把它放在椅子上或桌子上。

segments.en: Never never on the floor.
segments.zh: 永远不要在地板上。

segments.en: They're very superstitious about this.
segments.zh: 她们对此非常迷信。
